newsitem.title: USA: Florida to sell $765 mln transportation bonds.
newsitem.headline: Florida to sell $765 mln transportation bonds.

text.p: The Florida Department of Transportation plans to issue three series of bonds totalling about $765 million over the next nine months, a department finance planner said Thursday.
All three are 30-year issues that will be sold by competitive bid through the state Division of Bond Finance.

The department already has approval for a $350 million of general obligation bonds for highway rights of way and bridge construction. Those will probably be sold in July or August, DOT finance analyst Edward McCaron said.
Debt service on those bonds is paid from gasoline tax revenues via Florida's Transportation Trust Fund.

Two toll revenue bond issues will go before the state Board of Administration for final approval on June 12. Those are $65 million of Alligator Alley Revenue Bonds and $350 million Turnpike Revenue Bonds.
McCaron described both as "just plain vanilla." He said the state expects to send out preliminary offering statements this week for the Alligator Alley issue.
"We'd like to get that done in June if possible," he said.
Alligator Alley is the main thoroughfare through the Everglades and cuts across the southern tip of the state from Fort Lauderdale to Naples. It has no debt outstanding, McCaron said.

The bonds will finance construction of new toll plazas, roadside recreation areas and improvements at the intersection of State Road 29. Once the new toll plazas are built, motorists will stop once to pay a $1.50 toll instead of stopping twice to pay two 75-cent tolls.

The turnpike bonds are expected to be sold in March 1998, McCaron said. Although the turnpike is a long-established credit with about $1.1 billion of debt outstanding, that issue will require court validation.

The Legislature raised the turnpike's total debt cap to $1.5 billion from $1.1 billion last year. But the department has only $250 million of unused auhtorization remaining under the previous validation, McCaron said.
That issue will fund various improvements, including extension of the turnpike in the Tampa area, McCaron said.
None of the issues have been rated yet but McCaron said the state expects a double-A rating for the general obligation issue and single-A ratings for the two revenue bond issues.
The decision on whether to insure the issues will be left to the underwriters, he said.
